newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The government's decision yesterday to spend a further three trillion drachmas on arms by the year 2007 is a further burden on attempts by the Greek economy to achieve convergence with European countries.

--Three people hold the key to uncovering the details of the scandal at the Athens Stock Exchange and are expected to appear before judicial officials in the next few days. The bourse, meanwhile, traded yesterday with the participation of 50 of the 65 active firms, with more participation expected today.

--The day of the 1997 budget is near: National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou is expected the get the final okay to print out the budget at today's meeting with Prime Minister Costas Simitis.
--The labour, national economy and development ministries reluctant to legislate on new trading hours proposal that will keep stores open on weekdays up to 8.30 pm and on Saturdays until 4 pm.
--OECD officials urge the government to implement economic measures immediately after a lightning visit to Athens. Sources say the officials met Tuesday with leading government economic officials.
--The titles depository reacts sluggishly to the demand to clear titles and transactions yesterday.
--The finance ministry is planning surprises for the interest rates on its planned auction of five-year fixed and variable interest bonds next week.
--The market has not yet ruled out new developments in the 'Delta affair': as the deadline for clearing transactions ends this morning, another ten members face difficulties.

--The ministry will base the calculation of objective tax criteria - which calculates minimum taxable income and tax brackets - on 1994 real estate values for merchants and self-employed professionals.

--Brainstorming at the finance and national economy ministry has led to ideas to increase revenues above the initially forecast target of 8.5 trillion drachmas, with revenues touching the 15 percent mark and spending not exceeding 6.1 percent.
--Yesterday's session at the bourse was conducted amidst concerns and claims of a cover up. There were intense criticism of the procedures to clear transactions.
--The government's new fiscal measures will carry the ruling party PASOK's seal of approval following the decision to allow their examination by party bodies before the government's final approval.

--Inflows of 600 million dollars as the bourse resumed trading. The Bank of Greece proceeds with decisions aimed at facilitating the normal clearance of transactions at the ASE, including changes to the time limit. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
